answer: A farm running 194 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the yarrow stake is held until the vine settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the nectar audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 43% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
